a_records.quote: Lemma 4.14. (Müller and Scarsini, 2000) Let X, Y be two bivariate random vectors and have the same marginals, then X ≤sm Y is equivalent to X ≤uo Y.

hypotheses.text: X, Y bivariate with same marginals

conclusion.direction: X ≤_sm Y ⟺ X ≤_uo Y (supermodular = upper orthant in bivariate case)

a_records.quote: Theorem 4.15. Let Y1, Y2 follow (18). The following statements are true: (1) If µ2 + β(z)δ2 ≥ µ1 + β(z)δ1 for all z, σ1,ii = σ2,ii for all 1 ≤ i ≤ n and σ1,ij ≤ σ2,ij for all 1 ≤ i ≠ j ≤ n, then Y1 ≤uo Y2. (2) If Y1 ≤uo Y2 and g satisfies Assumption 4.1, then µ1 + E(β(Z))δ1 ≤ µ2 + E(β(Z))δ2 and σ1,ii = σ2,ii for all 1 ≤ i ≤ n. (3) If Y1 and Y2 have the same marginals and Y1 ≤uo Y2, then σ1,ij ≤ σ2,ij for all 1 ≤ i < j ≤ n.
a_records.compared: Y1 vs Y2 in upper orthant order

conclusion.direction: Y1 ≤_uo Y2 (sufficiency); necessity of mean-type inequality, equal diagonal variances and σ-inequalities

a_records.quote: Theorem 4.16. Let Y1, Y2 follow (18). The following statements are true: (1) If µ1 = µ2, δ1 = δ2 and Σ2 − Σ1 is copositive, then Y1 ≤cp Y2. (2) If µ1 = µ2, then Y1 ≤cp Y2, if and only if δ1 = δ2 and Σ2 − Σ1 is copositive. (3) If δ1 = δ2, then Y1 ≤cp Y2, if and only if µ1 = µ2 and Σ2 − Σ1 is copositive.
